children.value: This directory organizes engineering learning resources, research references, and technical study paths across the enterprise knowledge base. It is intended to help readers move from foundational coursework to specialized engineering domains without duplicating the source material maintained in each topic area.
: circuits, signals, electronics, power systems, and physical-layer design
: materials science, nanotechnology, structural behavior, and device materials
: mechanical design, aerospace systems, satellites, and structures
: biomedical systems, biotechnology, diagnostics, and neural engineering
: communications, spectrum, routing, and next-generation wireless systems
: nuclear systems, controls, safety, and energy-related engineering references
: quantum information, quantum networks, and quantum-enabled medical systems
: autonomous systems, intelligent devices, perception, and control
These engineering areas are not independent silos. They work together in real systems:
Electrical engineering provides the power, sensing, signal, and control foundations
Mechanical engineering provides the physical structure, motion, and system dynamics
Materials engineering defines what is physically possible in devices and structures
Network engineering routes information across distributed systems
Robotics integrates sensing, actuation, computation, and control into autonomous machines
Medical engineering applies these systems to human health and clinical needs
Nuclear and quantum engineering extend the same framework to high-risk, high-precision, and advanced-energy problems

The links below provide the shared academic foundation for this area, including computing, mathematics, physics, probability, machine learning, electronics, robotics, communications, and materials science. Topic-specific documentation should remain in the relevant subdirectory so that this index can serve as an entry point rather than a duplicate reference.
